head: WORKTREE
summary: POST /transactions is implemented as briefed: domain validation first, account/currency checks before writes, postings then atomic counter UPDATEs in ascending account order, all inside one @Transactional use case. Rejections and a mid-transaction rollback are proven at HTTP level. Only minor test-strength gaps remain.

acceptance_criteria.evidence: RecordTransactionService.record @Transactional; BalancePersistenceAdapter.apply atomic UPDATE; RecordTransactionServiceTest#appliesEachLineToItsAccountInAscendingAccountIdOrderAfterSavingThePostings; BalancePersistenceAdapterIT apply tests

findings.description: expectNothingPersisted checks postings and counters only; B3 says no row in transactions/postings. A rejection path that inserted a transactions row without postings would pass. Only the rollback test compares the transactions count.
findings.suggestion: Also assert the global transactions row count is unchanged in expectNothingPersisted (capture before the request).

findings.description: Location points to /transactions/{id}, but no GET endpoint exists yet, so the URI is dangling until a later task.
findings.suggestion: Note it in the 201 header description or track the GET in the roadmap.
